content: The A1C test is the primary method used to evaluate glycemic control in both clinical practice and research settings. It provides an estimate of an individual’s average blood glucose levels over the preceding two to three months. This measurement is strongly correlated with the risk of developing diabetes-related complications. Routine A1C testing is recommended for all individuals diagnosed with diabetes, both at the time of initial assessment and as part of their ongoing care. For patients with stable glycemic control, testing twice annually may be sufficient. However, for those with unstable glycemic control or those undergoing adjustments to their treatment regimen, testing every three months is advised.
